name: Iseltal
kurzbeschreibung: The Iseltal Valley in East Tirol is shaped by the Alps' last undammed glacial river, featuring dynamic gravel floodplains, dramatic side valleys, and the famed Iseltrail.
preis: Valley trails freely accessible; guided national park tours and attractions apply individual fees
oeffnungszeiten: Open year-round; prime hiking season runs May through October
beschreibung:
Überblick

The magnificent Iseltal Valley forms the geographical and ecological backbone of East Tirol. Tracing the untamed path of the River Isel – which, at 57 kilometres, represents the last entirely free-flowing, unfragmented glacial torrent in the entire Eastern Alps – the valley extends from the sunny alpine hub of Lienz up into the high-alpine heart of the Hohe Tauern National Park near Matrei. The sweeping glacial trough captivates with wild braided river gravels, rare riparian flora including the endangered German tamarisk, and soaring peaks of the Venediger and Schober ranges. By balancing thundering glacier-fed rapids with time-honored alpine hamlets and untouched biodiversity, the Iseltal stands as an ecological jewel. Whether embarking on serene riverbank walks, conquering challenging side valleys, or savoring genuine East Tyrolean mountain hospitality, visitors are captivated year-round by its pristine wilderness and open alpine vistas.

Route & Anforderungen

The crown jewel for hikers is the acclaimed 'Iseltrail'. Spanning roughly 75 kilometres across five scenic stages, this premier long-distance route tracks the river from its confluence in Lienz (673 m) directly up to the glacial snout of the Umbalkees ice sheet above 2,500 metres. Day-trippers and families will find the gentle lower valley legs between Lienz, St. Johann im Walde, and Huben ideal for relaxed walks and cycling on flat, crushed-gravel pathways. Casual sports shoes suffice for valley-floor itineraries. Conversely, ascending into the upper glaciated reaches or exploring the mighty Umbal Falls demands ankle-high hiking boots with deep rubber lugs, layered waterproof outerwear, and steady mountain footing.

Besuch & Anreise

Motorists access the valley via the Felbertauern highway B108 linking Mittersill in Salzburg with Lienz, or via federal road B100 along the Drau Valley. Train travelers arrive at Lienz railway station and take advantage of synchronized VVT bus connections serving all valley settlements.

Tipps

Do not miss visiting the roaring Umbal Falls in the upper Virgental tributary near Prägraten. Specially engineered cantilevered viewing decks extend directly over plunging glacial cascades, offering exhilarating perspectives of raw hydraulic power.
